judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional organisation and good standing representation for two entities, with the usual Material Adverse Effect carve-out; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes representations on behalf of 'Clearwire Parent', which the preamble does not name as a Party and which does not sign, so the source and enforceability of the Parent's representation is unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate authorisation and enforceability; the only oddity is that the enforceability sentence covers 'Clearwire' alone after the power clause covered both entities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same Clearwire Parent problem as Section 6.01: the preamble defines only two Parties while Section 7.02 also imposes covenants on the Parent, leaving its contractual status unexplained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Neither of the execution and delivery ... nor the compliance' is grammatically defective but the meaning survives; the rest is standard no-conflict language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It omits Clearwire Parent although Section 6.02 brought the Parent in, and its structure otherwise mirrors Section 5.03(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-consents representation with a specific, named exception for FCC spectrum lease applications; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is repeated verbatim at the end of Section 6.05 and is consistent with Section 7.01's consents covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lead-in qualifier is 'materially adverse effect on the ability of Clearwire to close', a narrower and differently-worded standard than the defined Clearwire Material Adverse Effect used elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.04 uses a different formulation for Licensee, and Section 8.02 disregards materiality qualifiers when computing Damages, but neither creates a hard contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Has complied in all respects with all federal, state, and local laws' followed immediately by a materiality carve-out is internally inconsistent phrasing, and the stray double comma before the FCC exception is a mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Section 5.05's structure and the FCC filing exception in Section 6.03(b); Section 8.02 again strips the materiality qualifier for damages purposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat brokers representation with no qualifiers; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 5.06 and nothing else in the instrument addresses brokers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mutual commercially-reasonable-efforts consents covenant; the two sentences are near-duplicates and the standard is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.04 imposes 'reasonable best efforts' and Section 7.07 'commercially reasonable best efforts' for overlapping cooperation duties, so three different standards coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is what the notifying party itself 'determines is reasonably likely to constitute a breach', a subjective condition that could be read to make the duty largely self-policing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes an obligation on Clearwire Parent, which the preamble does not make a Party, and it sits alongside Section 9.02's separate Event of Default definition without linking to it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening scope sentence limits the section to spectrum 'not ... subject to an IUA', yet the body immediately assumes Clearwire's obligation to meet the substantial service requirement on the licensed spectrum — a scope that fights its own content; 'knowingly or negligently' and 'material risk' add further softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the Initial Spectrum Capacity is under IUAs from the Effective Date, the scoping sentence read literally leaves this central covenant applying to almost nothing, which is hard to reconcile with Sections 1.01(a) and 7.05.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is scoped to non-IUA spectrum, but its final sentence grants a general right to 'sell, assign, sublease, delegate or transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder' to affiliates — a whole-agreement assignment right sitting inside an FCC-licence provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That free affiliate transfer right is in tension with Section 10.09's 'permitted assigns' (which nowhere defines what is permitted) and could be used to route around the Section 1.04 ROFR and Section 1.02(b) Option, which by their terms apply to Licensee 'or any of its Affiliates'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Parties believe that the provisions of this Agreement comply with all current FCC rules' is a statement of belief rather than a promise, and the covenant 'not to express any contrary view to regulatory agencies' is broad and of uncertain scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.03(a) contemplates jointly approaching the FCC for clarification when rules change, which assumes the ability to raise doubts with the regulator this section discourages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clearwire assumes 'all fees and taxes (now existing or hereafter arising) imposed on Licensee as a result of the licensing, regulation or use of Licensee's EBS Spectrum by Clearwire or Licensee' — an open-ended assumption including taxes triggered by Licensee's own use, and 'Licensee's EBS Spectrum' is not a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.01 separately allocates transfer-type taxes to Clearwire 'in connection with the Transactions', and the duration here ('until the end of the term of the IUA that is the last to expire') outruns the Section 9.01 Term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A covenant 'to preserve the intent of the relationships reflected in this Agreement to their mutual advantage' using 'commercially reasonable best efforts' is aspirational and supplies no ascertainable obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It invites a court to supply content from the parties' 'initial intent', which pushes against Section 10.03's entire-agreement clause and Section 10.05's direction that headings get no interpretive effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (iii) sweeps in anything 'otherwise related to the activities of Clearwire, any of its Affiliates or any of its sublicensees or resellers including, without limitation, damage to health' — a general catch-all with a single odd specific appended, exactly the ejusdem generis problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.03's deductible applies only to limb (i), so limbs (ii) and (iii) are uncapped, and Section 8.02 defines Damages expansively; that combination is coherent but very one-sided.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in 'statutory or regulatory compliance requirements' and items 'contingent or otherwise', which is broad to the point that what counts as a compensable Damage is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its second sentence deletes the materiality and knowledge qualifiers that Sections 5.05, 5.07, 6.05 and 6.04 were carefully drafted to include, so the bargained qualifiers survive for breach but not for recovery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section applies by its terms only to Sections 8.01(a)(i) and 8.01(b)(i) — representation and warranty claims — yet its threshold language also speaks of 'the breach of any covenant', which those subsections do not cover.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Covenant breaches live in Sections 8.01(a)(ii) and 8.01(b)(ii), which this section does not reference, so whether the $10,000 Deductible reaches covenant claims cannot be resolved from the four corners of Article VIII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably and promptly cause written notice', 'reasonably satisfactory' counsel and the reimbursement duty that applies even where the indemnifying party 'contests its obligation to indemnify' are soft points in an otherwise mechanical procedure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs alongside Section 8.04(c), which expressly forgives late notice absent prejudice, and Section 8.03's deductible is disapplied here ('regardless of the Deductible'); those are drafted to fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple post-judgment notice mechanic; nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It follows on from Section 8.04(a) and does not disturb Section 10.10's cumulative remedies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual loss and prejudice as a result of such failure' is a familiar standard; the sentence is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Section 8.04(a)'s prompt-notice requirement rather than contradicting it, and the two read together sensibly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Term ends at the earlier of three events, one of which is the very repayment the Agreement requires on expiry, so the trigger is self-referential; 'except as it pertains to Puerto Rico' is an undefined carve-out and 'Title 7 ... of the United States Bankruptcy Code' should be Chapter 7.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be reconciled with Section 2.02, which says the Term is not deemed expired while Section 1.02(b) Option periods remain open, or with Section 1.02(d) and Section 9.03, which give inconsistent answers on whether Options survive expiry.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Event of Default' requires that a material failure occur 'in circumstances where such failure results in the inability of the other party to exercise its full rights', a compound and unmeasurable threshold; the second sentence about a 'Loss' is unrelated to defaults and defined only in the IUA.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.01 hangs the entire termination machinery on this definition, including a payment-default cure period, yet a mere non-payment may not obviously produce 'inability ... to exercise full rights' — so the two provisions do not mesh.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The counterfactual 'or would have occurred, if Licensee complied in full with the requirements of this Agreement' extends survival to events that never happened, which is broad and hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly contradicts Section 1.02(d), under which 'any outstanding Options shall lapse automatically upon the expiration of the Term' unless Clearwire has already given notice of exercise, and it feeds Section 2.02's refund proviso.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional transfer-tax allocation; the enumerated list ends in 'or similar fees or taxes or governmental charges', a catch-all of modest reach, and 'Licensee(s) Indemnified Parties' is a typographical slip on the defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 7.06, which already makes Clearwire liable for fees and taxes imposed on Licensee, with a different temporal scope ('in connection with the Transactions' versus until the last IUA expires).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All agreements and covenants contained herein shall survive indefinitely until, by their respective terms, they are no longer operative' is self-cancelling phrasing, and the one-year survival runs from a Closing Date that varies by IUA.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.03 states a different survival rule keyed to the nature of the obligation, and Section 8.03's deductible for representation claims must be read against a one-year window that may expire before a claim matures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard integration and no-waiver language; 'with respect to the subject matter hereof' is the usual limiting phrase and the amendment formality is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The IUAs, Stock Pledge Agreement and Collateral Documents are separate instruments contemplated by Sections 1.02(a), 1.03 and 4.01(a), and Section 3.02(b) incorporates Clearwire's external Acceptable Use Policy, so what the integration clause actually absorbs is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain New York choice-of-law clause with an express exclusion of renvoi; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision selects a different law; Section 10.11's dispute procedure is procedural rather than substantive.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence direction that headings carry no interpretive weight; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matters because several headings in this instrument overpromise (notably Section 10.09 'Binding Effect; Assignment'), but the direction itself is consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Deemed given when delivered personally or by overnight courier, or mailed by certified mail' leaves it open whether certified mail is effective on mailing or on delivery, and the parenthetical facsimile requirement reads as mandatory without stating the consequence of omission.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Notices trigger cure periods in Section 9.01, ROFR and Option clocks in Sections 1.02(b) and 1.04, and the five-day Disqualification notice in Section 7.03, so timing here has knock-on effects, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent possible, allow the other Party reasonable time to comment' is soft, but the consent requirement and legal-disclosure exception are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the confidentiality and non-disclosure sections listed in the table of contents (11.14, 11.15) that do not appear in the operative text of this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare two-line severability clause with no reformation, no essential-terms exception and no 'to the extent' language, so it appears to preserve the rest of the deal even if a core payment or refund term fails — short clauses like this are exactly where construction fights start.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: If Section 2.02's refund mechanic or Section 1.02(b)'s price-to-be-negotiated Option were held unenforceable, this clause would purport to keep the remainder alive, which is hard to square with the recital that the Agreement 'would not have been executed but for all of the elements of the Total Consideration'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading promises assignment terms but the text says only that the Agreement binds 'successors and permitted assigns' without ever stating what assignment is permitted — a gap the provision itself does not fill.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The only assignment permission in the instrument is buried in Section 7.04, a section expressly scoped to spectrum not subject to an IUA, so whether Licensee may assign the Agreement as a whole cannot be answered without reconciling the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It declares that 'monetary damages alone will not be adequate' and then in the next breath lists 'money damages' among available remedies, and 'Notwithstanding any other provision herein' is an unbounded override.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cumulative-remedies override collides with Section 10.11(a), which makes the Dispute Resolution Procedures 'their sole means of' resolving disputes, and with Article VIII's indemnification architecture including the Section 8.03 Deductible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence at 'as their sole means of', so the operative scope of the exclusivity — and what it is the sole means of doing — is literally missing from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Sole means' cuts against Section 10.10's cumulative remedies and specific performance right, and Sections 1.04, 3.03(a) and 3.03(b) all refer disputes to 'arbitration under this Agreement' or 'the Dispute Resolution Procedure' whose terms this truncated section never supplies.
